dish: banh khot (crisp shrimp-topped mini rice pancakes)
address: 14 Nguyen Truong To, Ward 2, Vung Tau, Vietnam
w: The most famous banh khot house in Vung Tau, the city that owns the dish: tiny turmeric-coconut rice pancakes crowned with fresh shrimp, wood-fired by a line of women and wrapped in mustard leaf with herbs and nuoc cham. One of the oldest, and always a queue. ~07:00-14:00.

address: Phu My Hung (Sky Garden / Hung Gia), District 7, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: Saigon's Koreatown: the Sky Garden / Hung Gia blocks of Phu My Hung, home to ~20,000 Korean residents and a dense run of authentic Korean BBQ joints, soft-tofu-stew and cold-noodle houses, K-cafes and K-beauty shops - the real thing, run for the community.

dish: fresh market seafood cooked on the spot
address: Xom Luoi, Ward 2, Vung Tau, Vietnam
w: The locals' seafood market where the day's catch lands each afternoon (~15:00-16:00): pick prawns, crab, snails and fish from the tanks and have a stall grill or steam them on the spot for a small fee - Vung Tau's cheapest, freshest seafood feed.

dish: banh cong (crisp mung-bean, pork & shrimp fritter)
address: Dai Tam, My Xuyen, Can Tho, Vietnam
w: A ~100-year-old Mekong specialty: a deep-fried mung-bean, pork and whole-shrimp fritter eaten with herbs and sweet-sour sauce, at its source in the old Khmer village of Dai Tam (formerly Soc Trang). A cluster of ~15 family stalls near Dai Tam market, from mid-morning.
